QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_13

question.text: What is the ELM rate for equity index derivatives vs. individual stock derivatives?

answer.text: 2% for index derivatives and 3.5% for individual stock derivatives
3.5% for both index and individual stock derivatives
1% for index derivatives and 2% for individual stock derivatives
5% for index derivatives and 7% for individual stock derivatives

explanation.text: The Logic: In Indian equity derivative segments, Exposure Margin (ELM) is levied in addition to SPAN initial margin. It is conventionally set at 2% of the notional value of the contract for index futures/options and at 3.5% of notional for individual stock futures/options. The higher rate for single-stock contracts compensates for the higher idiosyncratic and tail risk of single stocks relative to diversified indices. The Trap: A flat 3.5% applied to both index and stock derivatives ignores the index-vs-single-stock distinction. 1% is the ELM rate associated with currency derivatives, not equity. The 5%/7% pair is not the prevailing equity ELM structure. Note: The 2% index / 3.5% stock-derivative ELM split was not located in the cited Series VIII pages (p.160-p.164, p.172), which describe SPAN initial margin, exposure margin, and the additional 2% tail-risk margin on short options at expiry; nor in the candidate currency (p.175-p.176) or interest-rate (p.256-p.257) pages. The framing above is general Indian equity-derivative margining knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
